summary.intent: Address the open finding (Low severity, button_latch.c:29) on Entire trail #3 for branch feature/step1-batch2, then commit and push the fix to PR #9 at the user's request.
summary.outcome: Fixed the race between button_latch_sample() and button_latch_take() with a small spin lock. Added a two-thread stress test that failed on the old code and passed 5 of 5 runs after the fix. Host suite passed 88/88 and the device build succeeded. Resolved the finding on the trail, then committed (45f9b60), pushed, and refreshed the trail and PR descriptions.

repo: Button latch code in firmware/src/runner/button_latch.{c,h} is shared between core 0 and core 1, so pending and first_ms must change together.
Host tests live in firmware/test/ (for example test_buttons) and the device firmware has a separate build. Both were run after touching shared code.
The Entire trail for a branch carries findings, gates (findings, approvals, CI) and a resolved-finding state. A resolved finding turns 'stale' when its line changes and is not reopened.
The skill workflow leaves fixes uncommitted and unpushed until the user approves. This conflicts with the user's 'commit frequently' rule, and the user chose to commit and push explicitly.

code.finding: A race existed between sample() and take(). If take() drained pending and sample() then added a new press, first_ms still held the previous press's time. The next take() reported a stale began_ms, which only affected the press_waited diagnostic. take() could also read first_ms while sample() rewrote it. A tiny spin lock around the accept step in sample() and around take() fixes both.

workflow: For race conditions, write a stress test first and watch it fail on the unfixed code. Here it failed on every run with 230k-250k stale reports. Then confirm it passes repeatedly after the fix, five runs in a row.
After pushing, update PR and trail descriptions so test-plan claims stay accurate. For example, the 'flashed and run on device' claim was corrected to exclude the last commit.
Defaulting to the trail for the current branch when none is specified worked well.

friction: The finding's resolution note on the trail says 'not yet committed or pushed'. That became stale after the push, and it can't be edited easily.
The PR test plan overstated device verification and had to be corrected after the push.
The skill's no-commit rule conflicts with the user's 'commit frequently' rule, and the assistant had to explain the conflict and ask.
